A 74-year-old married man residing with his partner works as a self-employed contractor in carpentry. Despite mild osteoarthritis, he maintains a rigorous exercise routine, completing five-kilometre runs three times weekly. His medical background includes hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and obesity (BMI >30). Current pharmacotherapy comprises amlodipine, valsartan, atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, and paracetamol PRN. He is an ex-smoker with a cumulative exposure of 31 pack-years, having successfully ceased smoking in 2023. Lower urinary tract symptoms are present, quantified by an IPSS score of 14, though he denies haematuria, skeletal discomfort, or unexplained weight loss. Weekly alcohol intake reaches approximately 39 units. A recent pulmonary function assessment was conducted for routine COPD surveillance. Commuting over an hour by rail, he manages his daily medications independently, relying on his spouse for logistical support.

DRE: The gland presents as symmetrically enlarged, possessing a firm, smooth surface devoid of palpable irregularities or asymmetry. Systemic review remains unremarkable; vital parameters are stable, and examination reveals no peripheral lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses.
